newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - Firm tone after holiday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - Firm tone after holiday.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds displayed a firmer tone as trade began after the July 4th Independence Day holiday, with prices at the long end marked up about an eighth of a point, largely due gains achieved by Treasuries.

Whether the municipal market will keep bounding higher after last week's big rally remained to be seen, with some traders questioning how much appetite retail investors would have, given how much yields have weakened.

"I think that it's going to be a little bit a grind from here. A lot of what had been driving the municipal market is redemptions in June, July and August. A lot of retail guys do trades weeks in advance," a trader said.
And traders cautioned that the market's firmer tone had yet to be confirmed by trades at the higher levels, as the market still was waking up after the three-day holiday.
Municipal bond sales this week were expected to total $2.1 billion in 99 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings added up to $1.3 billion in 41 sales, with a $150 million Sacramento Municipal Utility District, Calif., deal through Goldman, Sachs & Co., topping the list.
On the competitive side, 58 sales totaling $793 million were scheduled. A $265 million Washington deal on Wednesday is the largest.
An additional seven sales totaling $502 million were on the possible calender, meaning underwriters have said they might price the issues next week depending on market conditions.
In the secondary market, Allegheny, County, Pennsylvania, Sanitary Authority Sewer Revenues of 2024, which pay a 5-3/8 percent coupon, were bid at 5.55 percent, NET unchanged.
And Detroit, Michigan, Sewer Revenues of 2022, which pay a five percent coupon, were bid at 5.51 percent, NET, down one basis point.

September Treasury bond futures rose seven ticks to 113-13/32, while September municipal bond futures climbed nine ticks to 118-30/32. This left the MOB spread between the two futures contracts at plus 177 ticks.
